title: Chat agents: real status after an answer, stop closes the tab, cancelled questions, start errors
story: With the chat view on, an agent's tab now tells the truth. After answering a question or allowing a tool, the 'waiting for you' dot goes instead of staying on while the agent works. A question the agent withdraws no longer leaves dead buttons, stopping a chat agent closes its tab, and a failed Claude Code start shows its own error lines instead of a tab that silently vanishes.

checks.criterion: After an answer, allow or deny, the tab shows the agent working until it next waits or ends its turn; tool events count as work
checks.steps: Start Grillo with GRILLO_AGENT_RUNTIME=chat, open a made-up project, open a generic agent with '+'. Ask it: 'Ask me Red or Blue with AskUserQuestion'. Click 'Blue'.
checks.expected: The dot shows while the question waits and goes the moment you click; it returns only when the agent's turn ends or it asks again.

checks.criterion: Stopping a chat agent removes its tab
checks.steps: Open a generic chat agent tab, then call agent-chat:stop with that tab's id from the renderer devtools console (no button exists).
checks.expected: The tab leaves the tab bar, and the body says 'This agent is not running.'

checks.criterion: A cancel request for a pending question removes that question's answer buttons
checks.steps: Have the agent ask a clickable question. Interrupt it before answering, so Claude Code withdraws the question.
checks.expected: The option buttons disappear and 'The agent withdrew this question.' shows in their place.

checks.criterion: A failed start shows the last lines of Claude Code's own error text in the chat
checks.steps: Put a made-up 'claude' script first on PATH that prints 'Error: made-up failure' to stderr and exits 1. Start Grillo with the chat runtime and open a generic agent.
checks.expected: A red note with 'exit code 1' and 'Error: made-up failure'; after the tab closes, the same text under 'This agent is not running.'
